newsitem.title: USA: Globelle weighing sale of U.S. operations.
newsitem.headline: Globelle weighing sale of U.S. operations.

text.p: Globelle Corp, a Mississauga, Ont.,-based micro-computers distributor, said Saturday that it had formed a special committee of directors to consider strategic options regarding its U.S. operations, including an immediate sale of those operations.
In a statement, the company said it took the step because of continuing losses and deteriorating financial position of its U.S. operations.
"The board reached its decision after assessing the performance of U.S. operations and after considering a variety of restructuring alternatives," it said.
All of those alternatives woul have required a significant amount of additional investment by the company to support its U.S. business, said.

It said the committee has hired Nightingale & Associates LLC, A Stamford, Conn.,-based consulting firm, to help look for buyers and named Kevin Dowd, a principal at Nightingale, to be the president of its U.S. subsidiary, Globelle Inc.
Dowd replaces Christopher Rathgeber, who has been the subsidiary's president for the past four months. Rathgeber will continue to be chief financial officer of Globelle Corp, it said.

It said it has been advised that it was in default of a loan obtained in connection with its 1996 purchase of GBC Technologies Inc. The lenders are requiring that the U.S. subsidiary provide evidence of a commitment to refinance the loan by May 31 and that the loan by refinanced by July 28, it said.
Globelle said its Canadian loans are unaffected by the U.S. default.

Globelle previously said, in a report about its third quarter results, that it had written off $31 million of goodwill relating to its U.S. operations and recognized a $3.5 million provision for restructuring the business. It had also said it expects to incur further signficant restructuring charges and additional operating losses in the fourth quarter stemming from its U.S. business.
